## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

The packaged installer already writes `.hermes-bootstrap-complete`, so the post-install stamp has no effect on a normal install. The two parts that do change behavior, the pre-install stamp and the backfill migration, treat "`venv/bin/hermes --version` answers" as "install finished". That causes two problems described below. The PR also conflicts with current `quattro`, where this logic now lives in `omarchy-install-hermes-cli --now`.

**Verified:** the marker the helper writes (`schemaVersion: 1`, `pinnedCommit`, `pinnedBranch`, `completedAt`, no `desktopVersion`) matches upstream `write_bootstrap_marker` / `Write-BootstrapMarker` and passes the desktop app's marker validator. The write is atomic, an existing marker is never overwritten, and runtimes whose venv commands are missing or fail are left alone. Both PR tests pass at the PR head, and both fail against the merge-base code.

### The packaged `install.sh --skip-setup` already writes the marker

`hermes-desktop` 2026.8.31-3 builds from upstream [`29112bef`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/29112bef099274229cadff79cdff7bf7b99c4b77/scripts/install.sh#L3798-L3837) and installs its `scripts/install.sh` unchanged. In that file, `--skip-setup` only sets `RUN_SETUP=false`, which skips the setup wizard. `main()` still ends with the marker write:

```text
main()                               # scripts/install.sh @ 29112bef
  clone_repo
  setup_venv, install_deps           # venv/bin/hermes --version already answers here
  install_node_deps || return        # fatal on npm failure
  setup_path                         # writes ~/.local/bin/hermes
  run_setup_wizard                   # the only step --skip-setup skips
  print_success
  write_bootstrap_marker             # uses the --commit Omarchy passes
```

2026.9.7 (upstream `2237be35`) has the same call. On the merge-base, a marker missing after `install.sh` makes `omarchy install ai hermes` stop with "Hermes runtime setup did not complete" before launch, so the "finishes and launches without a marker" state in #12206 does not come from a completed run of this installer. The PR's install test only needs the new stamp because its mock `install.sh` was changed to stop writing the marker, which no longer matches the shipped installer.

**Impact:** the fresh-install path is unchanged in practice, and the tests now model an installer that differs from the shipped one.

**Suggested change:** restore the mock `install.sh` to write the marker as upstream does. Ask the reporter how their runtime was installed (for example, an older standalone Hermes install or an interrupted `install.sh`) to identify the actual markerless source.

### A failed or interrupted install is stamped complete and no longer retried

The pre-install stamp runs before `runtime_ready` and the repair guards. Upstream creates a working `venv/bin/hermes` several stages before the fatal Node step, `setup_path` and the marker, so an install that failed partway through passes the helper's `--version` probe.

| `install.sh` fails after the Python stage, then the user re-runs `omarchy install ai hermes` | Merge-base | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| `install.sh` runs again | yes | no, the runtime is stamped first |
| Result | install completes, `--check` passes | prints "Hermes Desktop has been installed." and launches, with no `~/.local/bin/hermes`, no Node deps, and a failing `--check` |
| Later re-runs | can repair | skip `install.sh`, because the marker now exists |

Reproduced in an isolated harness whose stub `install.sh` follows upstream `main()` stage order. Migration `1789746834.sh` stamps such runtimes in the same way.

**Impact:** the recovery described in the installer's own error message ("Re-run this command after resolving the installer error") stops working, and the marker no longer means the install finished, which the comment in `omarchy-install-hermes-cli` relies on.

**Suggested change:** do not stamp before the readiness and repair checks. Stamp only after an `install.sh` run has completed, or require stronger evidence than `hermes --version` that every upstream stage completed.

### Stamping a runtime the user installed makes Remove Hermes delete it

`omarchy-remove-ai-hermes` treats the marker as the only proof that Omarchy owns `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`, and deletes that checkout, `bootstrap-cache`, `bin` and `node` without prompting when the marker exists. `hermes-remove-test.sh` asserts that a runtime without the marker survives removal, local changes included. The migration's only ownership check is that the `hermes-desktop` package is present.

```text
user-installed ~/.hermes/hermes-agent (no marker, local commit) + hermes-desktop package
  without the migration → Remove Hermes keeps the runtime and the local commit
  with the migration    → marker written → Remove Hermes deletes the runtime and the local commit
```

The installer's pre-install stamp also leaves a marker when the same run then refuses the runtime ("moved beyond the packaged desktop release"). That marker's `pinnedCommit` is the package release, not the checkout's HEAD. Reproduced in the same isolated harness, default `~/.hermes` layout only.

**Impact:** on the default layout, removing Hermes can delete a user's own checkout and local work without asking.

**Suggested change:** backfill only runtimes with evidence that Omarchy installed them, never stamp ahead of the adoption and refusal checks, and add a test where a markerless user runtime survives the migration or an installer refusal followed by Remove Hermes.

### Rebase onto current `quattro`

`bin/omarchy-install-ai-hermes` on `quattro` is now a thin wrapper around `omarchy-install-hermes-cli --now`, and a trial merge conflicts in that file and in `test/shell.d/hermes-desktop-install-test.sh`. On `quattro`, `--check` also requires the seeded native app, so a backfilled marker alone does not make it pass for runtimes without that app.

**Note:** if a backfill is kept, it does not re-run `omarchy-theme-set-hermes --activate`, so a skin activation missed by the one-shot migration `1788619462.sh` only happens at the next theme change.
